steps.content:
N.F. 71, on the eve of DisCity's independence.

With the warfront collapsing, the Metropole Alliance was staring into the abyss of inevitable defeat.

After DisCity's forces intercepted a series of nuclear strikes, it became clear that only a weapon capable of countering their anomalous power wielders could change the course of the war.

In a final, desperate gamble, the Metropole Alliance marshaled its remaining forces for a massive, surprise attack.

To shroud the operation in absolute secrecy, they turned to a team of elite cryptographers, tasking them with a new, unbreakable cipher. They called it—


<size=52>Monolith</size>.
[Radio]
The Monolith awaits. Report immediately.
[Scene Change: Mountain Path]
The evening is cloudy, with a fine, sparse rain drifting in the air.
You trudge up the rugged, muddy path toward the hilltop manor. In the distance, the purr of luxury cars echoes, but none turn onto this forgotten track.
This is DisCity's remote outskirts, where the roads remain stubbornly wild. In the failing twilight, the shadows of withered trees sway, weaving an atmosphere thick with unease.
—A perfect hideout for spies, you think.
Leaning against a gnarled tree to catch your breath, you finally manage to flag down a passing car.

steps.speaker: Unassuming Young Man
steps.content: Hi... you... you can see me? Are you alright?
The window slides down to reveal a man in his twenties, so thoroughly ordinary he's almost invisible. His face is the kind you forget the moment you look away.
But his presence here, now, tells you everything. You're almost certain he's another Outland spy, here for the Monolith.
A ride is an obvious advantage. And if you can turn the journey into an opportunity to gather information, infiltrating the manor will be that much simpler.

steps.speaker: Unassuming Young Man
steps.content: Oh... you got this telegram too. Well, it seems we're in the same line of work.

steps.speaker: Unassuming Young Man
steps.content: Vilensoff? Not many know about that place. If you don't mind me asking, what brings you out this way?
As he speaks, the young man's fingers stray absently toward his breast pocket. A gun? A transmitter?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Because I received a secret telegram.

steps.speaker: Unassuming Young Man
steps.content: That's it... Well, it seems we're in the same line of work.

steps.speaker: Unassuming Young Man
steps.content: Get in. I'll take you there. And if you don't mind, I've got some spare clothes in the back.
steps.female_content: Get in. I'll take you there. And if you don't mind, I've got some of my girlfriend's spare clothes in the back.

steps.content: [Scene Transition: Car Interior]
You quickly change into the spare clothes he provided in the back seat.
steps.female_content: To give you privacy, the young man steps out of the car and turns his back to the window. You quickly change into the spare clothes he provided in the back seat.

steps.content: The outfit is perfectly, extraordinarily ordinary, a mirror of the man himself. It's the kind of bland, nondescript attire that lets you vanish into a crowd the moment you look away.

steps.speaker: Edward
steps.content: The name's Edward Simmons. And you are? ...Oh, it's perfectly fine if you'd rather not answer. I understand. We're not exactly in a profession that encourages sharing.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: My name is ${PlayerName}.

steps.speaker: Edward
steps.content: Hmm... Can't say I've heard the name before, but then again, that doesn't mean much in our line of work. The name I just gave you isn't the one I was born with, either.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You can call me "Gray Coat."

steps.speaker: Edward
steps.content: Hmm, can't say I've heard the codename before, but then again, that doesn't mean much in our line of work. The name I just gave you isn't the one I was born with, either.

steps.speaker: Edward
steps.content: Honestly, by the time we get to the manor, I doubt we'll meet a single person who's using their real name.
Despite his claim that your profession doesn't really "encourage sharing," Edward proves to be a relentless chatterbox, probing you with casual conversation throughout the drive.
You offer cautious, non-committal replies at first, but soon realize it might just be his nature. Eventually, you close your eyes, feigning sleep to end the charade.
[Black Screen Transition: Manor Exterior]
The car rumbles to a halt at the manor gates after a half-hour journey.
The manor looms, a relic of brick and stone. Under the watchful eyes of two fully armed guards, you and Edward are ushered into the main hall.
[Manor Hall]
A handful of figures are already scattered through the hall.

Some observe from solitary perches; others speak in hushed tones within small circles. In both attire and manner, every person maintains a carefully constructed plainness—a collective effort to remain unmemorable.
The most fundamental rule of espionage is to blend in.
And now that rule applies to <color=#fb9259>you</color> as well.
A glance at your own outfit confirms it... Thanks to Edward, you are perfectly camouflaged.
This is Hilda's memory. LINK has recreated the pivotal days in this manor that culminated in the birth of "Monolith."
Your objective is to unearth her secrets and extract the vital intelligence from this period.
Now, you decide to...

options: Observe the people sitting alone in corners
Observe the people gathered in groups

steps.content: A grim-faced man with cropped hair occupies a corner. His bearing immediately sets him apart; he carries himself not like a bureaucrat, but with the sharp alertness of the room's guards, likely a soldier or field operative.
He fidgets incessantly: rolling an unlit cigarette between his fingers, his hand then straying to absently touch his collar.
In another corner, a short-haired young woman sits with unnerving stillness. Her sharp eyes have been actively scanning the room since she arrived, missing nothing.

options: Observe the people gathered in groups

steps.content: Nearby, a circle of socialites, draped in elegant attire, is chatting with practiced ease.

steps.speaker: Well-dressed Businessman
steps.content: Let's be pragmatic. The outcome on the front is a foregone conclusion... The question for the Alliance now isn't if, but how we negotiate our position with DisCity.

steps.speaker: Well-dressed Businessman
steps.content: No one seriously believes the "Monolith" is for fighting. It's a deterrent. A... well, a rather powerful bargaining chip, that's all.

steps.speaker: Elderly Scholar
steps.content: Mind your tone, Mr. Johnson. This is not the place for such defeatist talk.

steps.speaker: Elderly Scholar
steps.content: A single setback is not a surrender. Our intelligence operations have been cultivated for decades. We have the network, the resources to wage a protracted campaign from the shadows if it comes to that.

steps.speaker: Elderly Scholar
steps.content: Our resolve is our greatest weapon. We must not waver. Victory in the next phase depends on it.
A modest offering of coffee and sugar is laid out for guests.
The coffee is a bitter, dark liquid made from stewed lettuce, and the accompanying sugar cubes are just cheap, questionable candies—a telling detail of the shortages.
You've only just put down the dreadful cup when you glance up. A figure now stands on the second-floor staircase, looking down upon the hall.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: Good evening, ladies and gentlemen. I am Hilda Hartlein. My thanks to you all for accepting my invitation.
Her voice, cool and clear as a chime, cuts through the hall. Instantly, the room freezes, every gaze drawn to the top of the central staircase.
This is your first time seeing her true form, not as a prisoner in a canister, or a soul drowning in filth.

An oversized coat hangs from her slender frame, making her seem unbearably fragile. Her skin is deathly pale, almost translucent, and her eyes hold the eerie, grayish-red hue of a specter. Merely standing seems to require a monumental effort, as if a faint breeze could dissolve her into nothing.
She offers a slow, courteous bow to the assembled crowd.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: I know the "Monolith" is the subject on everyone's mind. But first, allow me to provide some necessary context for this gathering.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: Since the Nightfall, human civilization has suffered a devastating blow. We watched nations dissolve into scattered settlements and struggling city-states, each fighting for its own survival.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: It was Dr. Keylan's discovery of the Hypercube that finally reunited us. It gave us a common purpose: to build DisCity and forge the City-State Coalition. We were meant to stand as a unified front, a testament to humanity's resilience.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: We operated on a foundation of shared knowledge and rational trade. DisCity, as the sole source of Hypercubes, was a partner—not a master.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: But that foundation is now being deliberately dismantled.

A strategic wartime map unfolds behind her, detailing the metropoles and their territories. Several zones are highlighted in alarming red and orange, indicating active conflicts and military stalemates. Her red-gloved hand glides over the chart, bypassing other hotspots to settle unerringly on the most critical location in the bottom-right quadrant: DisCity.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: There are forces among us sowing division under the false banner of "independence." They are pitting brother against sister, severing the very bonds that made us strong.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: They have reignited old hatreds between city-states, reducing a united front to squabbling fragments. They profit from the chaos they create, while civilians pay the price, displaced by the flames of war.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: We cannot, and we will not, allow this to continue.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: However, our efforts have been compromised. A mole within our operation has been leaking Monolith intelligence, coordinating attacks against our interests.
The room holds its breath. But no one is surprised.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: To mitigate the ongoing security risk, I requested the relocation of the entire project. This "safe house" was selected for its defensibility and isolation, creating a contained environment to secure the Monolith's development.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: Now, with the Monolith in its final testing phase, I advised my superiors that we issue assistance directives laced with critical data to "invite" all of you here.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: It was, of course, a calculated risk. I am operating on the assumption that our mole would find such bait irresistible, and would inevitably be drawn into our midst. This presents our best opportunity to identify, capture, and eliminate the threat.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: Now, if you will all remain calm and in place, we will begin the verification process.
(Show individual portraits one after another)
An uncanny silence holds the room. Hilda descends the stairs, offering nods to a few—familiar faces—while approaching others for quiet inquiries.
You watch, your focus sharpening as you note her method: she uses gloved hands to briefly touch the hems or collars of their clothing, exchanging a hushed word before moving on.
Then, her path leads inevitably to you.

The memory of the fidgeting man, his collar his tell, clicks into place. A classic place for a poison pill. In a flash of insight, you palm the small candy from your pocket and covertly slide it into your own collar.
Hilda stands before you, her face a mask of confusion.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: ...You're a face I don't recognize. You weren't on my list. And you... you don't carry yourself like an agent or spy.
Her voice remains soft. She reaches out, not as a gesture of affection, but of inspection, neatly straightening your collar.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: Your poison pill is larger than standard issue. Not an expert at concealment, are you? You must be from a different agency... or something else entirely.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: So, let's not waste time. Who are you, truly?
You had the look, the mannerisms—enough to pass a casual inspection. But it's painfully clear that it isn't enough for Hilda. You need a story, an "identity" that fits into this web of deceit.

Everyone here is an undercover agent personally selected by her, each with a prior history with Monolith. You, an outsider who knows none of them and has never interacted with Monolith, need a plausible role. The most logical choice seems to be...

options: I'm an undercover agent, infiltrating the DisCity Intelligence Bureau.
I'm an "anomalous power expert" sent by the metropoles.
